answer: Each identity leases one shale core spanning the interval from a surveyed zenith marker to the tide line, locking 150 units for 12 epochs against it. Registrars hash its fracture map and length at lease; the registry refuses a core already leased, and splitting one core breaks fracture continuity, so pieces fail checks. Auditors rescan cores at low tide each epoch, comparing hash, length and custody log; a second claim on the same map is proof of reuse and voids that weight. The 150 returns after 12 clean epochs. Scaling to 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 distinct cores and 150,000 locked at once.
